newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavaria's Stoiber says Bonn must buy Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Bavaria's Stoiber says Bonn must buy Eurofighter.

text.p: Germany must make a firm order for the Eurofighter combat aircraft or risk the demise of its aerospace industry, Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber was quoted as saying on Monday.

Stoiber, whose home state is the heartland of the German aircraft and space industry, told Cologne's Express newspaper: "The Eurofighter is the key project for the German air, space and defence industry.
"If we said no to the Eurofighter, we would lose our capacity to cooperate in Europe in this sector," he said, adding that 18,000 jobs hung on the fate of the project.

Bonn is still struggling to put together the financing in its 1998 budget which would enable it to make a firm order for the 180 Eurofighters which Defence Minister Volker Ruehe wants to buy to modernise the German air force.
The total cost of Germany's Eurofighters would be 23 billion marks ($13.3 billion), and Finance Minister Theo Waigel is struggling to close a financing gap of two billion marks.

Ruehe has agreed to provide one billion marks out of his ministerial budget, while Waigel is negotiating with the German partner in the Eurofighter consortium -- Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) -- over redirecting pre-financing for DASA's Airbus operations to cover the remaining shortfall.

The news magazine Focus reported at the weekend that DASA chief executive Manfred Bischoff was due to hold talks with Waigel on the Eurofighter on Tuesday, but the a ministry spokesman could not confirm this.
Eurofighter groups DASA, a unit of carmaker Daimler-Benz AG, with British Aerospace, Alenia of Italy and state-owned CASA of Spain.
